function.description:
Purpose: Read the bound tab's current state without changing it, and mint short-lived 'ref' tokens for a following browser_act call — the only tool that mints refs.

When to use: Starting work on a page; discovering controls; right before a ref-based browser_act; after navigation or a big page change; after a stale/missing-ref error.

When not to use: Modifying the page (browser_act); changing location (browser_navigate); waiting (browser_wait); proving an outcome (browser_assert); screenshots/snapshots (browser_capture_evidence).

Important capabilities: 'compact' (default) returns a ref-tagged element list; 'aria' and 'text' describe the page but mint no refs.

Required sequencing: Observe before any ref-based act; use only the latest observationId/refs for this session; observe again after navigation or whenever a result reports the observation invalidated.

Important limitations: truncated=true on a large page means retry with a bigger maxNodes rather than guessing unseen content. 'aria'/'text' never produce refs. Only the bound tab is visible.

Expected result: observationId, snapshotId (traceability only), url, title, a snapshot string with inline '[ref_N] role "name"' tokens, and truncated.

Recommended next step: browser_act with a ref from this snapshot, or browser_assert if the needed fact is already visible here.
function.name: browser_observe

parameters.description: Read the page in an already-bound session. Does not modify the page or prove completion.

browserSessionId.description: An opaque AXIS tab handle returned by browser_tabs; never a raw Chrome tabId.

maxNodes.description: Max accessibility nodes in compact mode; raise only if a result reports truncated.

mode.description: compact for actionable refs; aria for accessibility structure; text for plain readable text.

function.description:
Purpose: Perform exactly one interaction — click, fill, press, hover, select, check, uncheck, upload, drag, or scroll — in the bound tab. One call is one interaction, never a batch.

When to use: One concrete interaction is needed now.

When not to use: Understanding an unknown page (browser_observe); going to a URL (browser_navigate); waiting for a resulting transition (browser_wait, afterward); confirming success (browser_assert — a successful act does not itself prove it); collecting evidence (browser_capture_evidence).

Important capabilities: Prefers a 'ref' from the latest browser_observe; falls back to a bounded 'locator'. Returns 'whatChanged' (URL/focus/popup deltas) when the bridge reports one.

Required sequencing: Observe first for ref-based actions; use only current refs. After acting, check 'observationInvalidated' — if true, observe again before the next ref-based action.

Important limitations: Never runs arbitrary JavaScript or a raw method. 'upload' and 'drag' have no ref-based method and need 'locator' (drag also needs 'targetLocator'). 'check'/'uncheck' are locator-only — the bridge has no deterministic ref-based check/uncheck (only a toggling click). 'hover' without a ref needs a CSS 'selector' in locator.

Expected result: action, whatChanged (may be null), observationInvalidated.

Recommended next step: browser_wait for an async transition; browser_assert to confirm; browser_observe if invalidated; browser_diagnose only after an unexpected failure.
function.name: browser_act

parameters.description: Perform exactly one interaction in the bound session. Does not verify business success.

action.description: click/fill/press/hover/select act on one element via 'ref' (preferred) or 'locator'. check/uncheck/upload/drag require 'locator' (drag also 'targetLocator') — no ref path exists for these four. scroll uses 'deltaX'/'deltaY', not a ref.

browserSessionId.description: An opaque AXIS tab handle returned by browser_tabs; never a raw Chrome tabId.

deltaX.description: Horizontal scroll distance in px (positive = right). Used only by 'scroll'.

deltaY.description: Vertical scroll distance in px (positive = down). Used only by 'scroll'.

files.description: Approved local file path(s) to upload. Required (non-empty) for 'upload'.

key.description: Key or shortcut (e.g. 'Enter', 'Control+A'). Required for 'press'; ignored otherwise.

locator.description: A semantic locator for one element, used when no ref applies. Supply at least one of 'selector' (CSS) or 'text'/'role'/'name'/'label'/'placeholder'. Use only values already seen (e.g. in browser_observe) or given by the user. Fallback/requirement for click/fill/press/hover/select/check/uncheck/upload; the drag source.

exact.description: Exact match instead of case-insensitive/substring. Default false.

name.description: Accessible name to match, typically with 'role'.

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. 'button', 'textbox'); combine with 'name'.

selector.description: A CSS selector for the element.

text.description: Visible text to match (e.g. a link/button label).

observationId.description: observationId that produced 'ref'; required with 'ref'. Must be the latest one for this session.

options.description: Option value(s)/label(s) to select, matching real options. Required (non-empty) for 'select'.

ref.description: A ref token from the latest browser_observe. Preferred for click/fill/press/hover/select; not usable for check/uncheck/upload/drag.

targetLocator.description: A semantic locator for one element, used when no ref applies. Supply at least one of 'selector' (CSS) or 'text'/'role'/'name'/'label'/'placeholder'. Use only values already seen (e.g. in browser_observe) or given by the user. The drag destination. Required for 'drag'; unused otherwise.

exact.description: Exact match instead of case-insensitive/substring. Default false.

name.description: Accessible name to match, typically with 'role'.

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. 'button', 'textbox'); combine with 'name'.

selector.description: A CSS selector for the element.

text.description: Visible text to match (e.g. a link/button label).

timeoutMs.description: Max wait for the target to become actionable, in ms (max 120000).

value.description: Text to type. Required for 'fill' (may be empty to clear); ignored otherwise.

function.description:
Purpose: Open a URL or change history (reload/back/forward) in the bound tab.

When to use: Direct URL or history control is intended.

When not to use: Clicking a link/button (browser_act); waiting for the destination to finish loading (browser_wait, afterward); confirming the destination (browser_assert); inspecting it (browser_observe).

Important capabilities: Returns resulting tab state and 'whatChanged' when available.

Required sequencing: Observe before interacting with the destination — every prior ref/observationId is invalid after this call.

Important limitations: Does not verify application-level success (a loaded page is not a verified outcome); does not touch page elements.

Expected result: resulting url/title, whatChanged, observationsInvalidated=true.

Recommended next step: browser_wait if still loading, then browser_observe, then browser_assert.
function.name: browser_navigate

parameters.description: Open a URL or change history in the bound tab. Invalidates every prior ref/observationId.

browserSessionId.description: An opaque AXIS tab handle returned by browser_tabs; never a raw Chrome tabId.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait for the navigation/history change, in ms (max 120000).

url.description: Absolute URL to open. Required when operation is 'open'; use a URL already known or observed.

function.description:
Purpose: Wait for one supported browser condition without asserting a business outcome.

When to use: Loading/rendering in progress; an element appearing/disappearing; a URL/navigation change; network idle; a popup, dialog, request, or response.

When not to use: An arbitrary sleep; proving completion (browser_assert, afterward); inspecting (browser_observe); acting (browser_act).

Important capabilities: A fixed set of conditions with a bounded timeout.

Required sequencing: Pick the most specific condition; assert or observe afterward as needed.

Important limitations: Success means only that the condition occurred, not that the outcome is correct — it is not an assertion; never runs arbitrary JavaScript.

Expected result: condition, matched=true, a bounded result payload, and observationsInvalidated for a confirmed navigation/url change.

Recommended next step: browser_assert to verify; browser_observe if the page changed; browser_diagnose only after an unexpected timeout.
function.name: browser_wait

parameters.description: Wait for one browser condition in the bound tab. Does not verify a business outcome.

browserSessionId.description: An opaque AXIS tab handle returned by browser_tabs; never a raw Chrome tabId.

condition.description: 'element_state' needs 'locator'+'state'. 'url'/'request'/'response'/'text' need 'expected' (URL substring, or literal text for 'text'). 'navigation'/'page_load'/'network_idle'/'popup'/'dialog' need only timeoutMs.

expected.description: URL substring or literal text to wait for; required by url/request/response/text.

locator.description: A semantic locator for one element, used when no ref applies. Supply at least one of 'selector' (CSS) or 'text'/'role'/'name'/'label'/'placeholder'. Use only values already seen (e.g. in browser_observe) or given by the user. Required for 'element_state'; unused otherwise.

exact.description: Exact match instead of case-insensitive/substring. Default false.

name.description: Accessible name to match, typically with 'role'.

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. 'button', 'textbox'); combine with 'name'.

selector.description: A CSS selector for the element.

text.description: Visible text to match (e.g. a link/button label).

state.description: Element state to wait for; used only with 'element_state'.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait for the condition, in ms (max 120000); fails with TIMEOUT on expiry.

function.description:
Purpose: Verify one expected page/element condition. The preferred way to confirm an action succeeded or an outcome was reached.

When to use: Confirming an action's effect; an element's visibility/state/value/text/count/attribute; the page title; the accessibility outline; proving a final outcome before reporting completion.

When not to use: Discovering unknown elements (browser_observe); mutating (browser_act); navigating (browser_navigate); diagnosing an unexpected failure (browser_diagnose); as a substitute for a still-needed browser_wait.

Important capabilities: A retrying bridge check with a bounded timeout, returning expected/actual and, on mismatch, bounded bridge diagnostic detail.

Required sequencing: Use a locator/expectation already known; a failed assertion (passed=false) is a valid, informative result, not a tool error.

Important limitations: Cannot discover unknown structure. Only a genuine condition-not-met mismatch is reported as ok:true/passed:false — scope, permission, input, and infrastructure errors remain ok:false.

Expected result: assertion, passed, the expected value as supplied, actual (when available), and diagnostic detail on mismatch.

Recommended next step: Report the outcome if passed; capture evidence or diagnose if not, before deciding whether to retry the underlying action.
function.name: browser_assert

parameters.description: Verify one expected condition in the bound tab; the preferred way to confirm an outcome.

assertion.description: 'visible'..'checked' plus 'value'/'text'/'count'/'attribute' are element assertions and need 'locator'. 'title' checks the page title against 'expected'. 'aria_snapshot' matches the accessibility outline.

attribute.description: Attribute name to read. Required when assertion is 'attribute'.

browserSessionId.description: An opaque AXIS tab handle returned by browser_tabs; never a raw Chrome tabId.

contains.description: Substring match instead of exact. Applies to 'text' and 'title' only.

count.description: Expected number of matching elements. Required when assertion is 'count'.

locator.description: A semantic locator for one element, used when no ref applies. Supply at least one of 'selector' (CSS) or 'text'/'role'/'name'/'label'/'placeholder'. Use only values already seen (e.g. in browser_observe) or given by the user. Required for every element assertion (all values except 'title'/'aria_snapshot').

exact.description: Exact match instead of case-insensitive/substring. Default false.

name.description: Accessible name to match, typically with 'role'.

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. 'button', 'textbox'); combine with 'name'.

selector.description: A CSS selector for the element.

text.description: Visible text to match (e.g. a link/button label).

timeoutMs.description: Max time to retry before reporting passed=false, in ms (max 120000).

function.description:
Purpose: Produce a bounded artifact — screenshot, DOM/accessibility snapshot, PDF, or trace — from the bound tab.

When to use: An explicit evidence request; preserving an important state; a failed assertion; diagnosis needing an artifact.

When not to use: Routine page understanding (browser_observe); by default after every action; acting or asserting; console/network diagnostics (browser_diagnose).

Important capabilities: Element screenshots are locator-based (no ref path). Large/binary results are saved to disk via the native host by default.

Required sequencing: Choose the smallest useful capture; chain trace_start -> actions -> trace_stop/trace_export using the returned traceId.

Important limitations: 'element_screenshot' requires 'locator'; 'trace_stop'/'trace_export' require 'traceId'. saveToDisk=false never returns a large payload to the LLM.

Expected result: evidenceId, capture type, url, capturedAt, and either saved=true+path/bytes/mimeType or saved=false+a bounded preview.

Recommended next step: Hand the path/metadata to the user, or browser_diagnose if it reveals a technical failure.
function.name: browser_capture_evidence

parameters.description: Produce a bounded evidence artifact from the bound tab. Not for routine page understanding.

browserSessionId.description: An opaque AXIS tab handle returned by browser_tabs; never a raw Chrome tabId.

capture.description: 'element_screenshot' requires 'locator'. 'trace_stop'/'trace_export' require 'traceId' from a prior 'trace_start'. Others need no extra args beyond filename/saveToDisk.

filename.description: Optional safe filename (no path separators or '..'); generated if omitted. Ignored when saveToDisk is false.

locator.description: A semantic locator for one element, used when no ref applies. Supply at least one of 'selector' (CSS) or 'text'/'role'/'name'/'label'/'placeholder'. Use only values already seen (e.g. in browser_observe) or given by the user. Required for 'element_screenshot' (locator-based, not ref-based).

exact.description: Exact match instead of case-insensitive/substring. Default false.

name.description: Accessible name to match, typically with 'role'.

role.description: ARIA role to match (e.g. 'button', 'textbox'); combine with 'name'.

selector.description: A CSS selector for the element.

text.description: Visible text to match (e.g. a link/button label).

saveToDisk.description: Save artifacts to disk via the native host (default true). False returns only bounded metadata/preview, never a large payload.

traceId.description: Trace id from a prior 'trace_start'. Required for 'trace_stop'/'trace_export'.

function.description:
Purpose: Investigate a technical failure, hang, or explicit diagnostic request in the bound tab.

When to use: An unexpected action/assertion failure; a stuck page; suspected console/network errors; trace status; an explicit diagnostic request.

When not to use: Normal observation/action/navigation/waiting; business-outcome verification (browser_assert); user-facing evidence (browser_capture_evidence).

Important capabilities: Bounded, redacted console/network reads; a DOM snapshot summary; trace status; response_body is opt-in and off by default.

Required sequencing: Pick the smallest diagnostic source likely to explain the specific problem observed.

Important limitations: response_body can still leak app-specific secrets beyond the redaction list even when enabled. Never modifies the page; does not replace browser_observe/browser_wait/browser_assert.

Expected result: diagnostic type, redactionApplied=true, bounded entries with a truncated flag.

Recommended next step: Retry only on a clearly transient signal; otherwise report or escalate.
function.name: browser_diagnose

parameters.description: Investigate a technical failure in the bound tab. Not for interaction, observation, or verification.

browserSessionId.description: An opaque AXIS tab handle returned by browser_tabs; never a raw Chrome tabId.

diagnostic.description: 'response_body' needs 'requestId' and is disabled unless the host enabled allow_response_body. 'console'/'network' return buffered events bounded by 'limit'. 'dom' returns a diagnostic snapshot summary. 'trace_status' optionally scoped by 'traceId'.

limit.description: Max buffered events to return. Used by 'console'/'network'.

requestId.description: Request id from a prior 'network' event. Required for 'response_body'.

traceId.description: Optional trace id to scope 'trace_status' to one trace.

function.description:
Purpose: Manage the Chrome tabs available to AXIS and obtain the trusted logical browserSessionId handles every other browser tool requires. AXIS has access to every ordinary tab the bridge exposes, not just one bound tab.

When to use: Discovering what tabs are open; opening a new tab for a task; switching which tab is active/focused; closing a tab you created or finished with.

When not to use: Reading a tab's content (browser_observe); interacting with page elements (browser_act); as a way to run arbitrary navigation (use browser_navigate on the resulting handle instead of relying on 'create's url).

Capabilities: 'list' refreshes from the bridge and returns every available tab with its handle, title, sanitized URL, and active state. 'create' opens a new tab (URL passes the configured firewall) and returns its new handle. 'activate' switches Chrome's focus to an existing handle. 'close' closes a handle's tab and invalidates only that tab's observations.

Required workflow: Call 'list' before assuming any specific handle exists; use the exact handle a prior 'list'/'create' returned for 'activate'/'close'; observe a tab again after activating it before element-targeted actions, since refs are only valid for the tab and observation that produced them.

Limitations: Never invent a handle or supply a raw Chrome tabId — only handles returned by this tool are valid. A fabricated, stale, or already-closed handle returns TAB_NOT_FOUND or TAB_CLOSED. The registry tracks a bounded number of tabs at once.

Expected result: 'list' returns tabs (each with browserSessionId/title/url/active); 'create'/'activate' return the affected browserSessionId and activated state; 'close' returns the closed handle and, when the bridge reports one, the newly active tab.

Common errors: TAB_NOT_FOUND (unknown handle), TAB_CLOSED (handle already closed), FIREWALL_DENIED (create's url blocked by policy), INVALID_ARGUMENT (missing browserSessionId for activate/close).

Recommended next step: browser_observe the tab you just created or activated before acting on it.
function.name: browser_tabs

parameters.description: Manage Chrome tabs available to AXIS. Use this tool to list, create, activate, or close tabs and to obtain trusted logical browserSessionId handles for the other browser tools. It never exposes raw Chrome identifiers.

browserSessionId.description: Opaque logical tab handle returned by browser_tabs list/create. Required for activate and close. Never invent it and never provide a raw Chrome tabId.

operation.description: Required operation. list returns available tabs and logical handles; create opens a new tab; activate switches Chrome focus to an existing logical tab; close closes a logical tab.

url.description: Optional initial URL for create. It must pass the configured firewall. Do not use it for activate or close.
